messages:
Sophia Patel: Brain dump: proposal to add an "edge quota steward" process in front of the runtime. Responsibilities: ultra-low-latency token checks, transient burst leases, connection fingerprinting, and conservative fallback if central broker is slow. Want to discuss interface and abuse mitigations.

Tom Nguyen: Sounds similar to previous ambassador idea but I want clearer invariants: what does the steward guarantee? eventual global correctness or only probabilistic?

Devin Brooks: Guarantee model: steward provides local decisions with two bounded guarantees: 1) short-term local burst up to lease when granted; 2) central ledger is authoritative over minutes. So correctness is eventual + safety if we can revoke leases quickly.

Carla Mendez: Telemetry first: emit these events: steward.request, steward.grant, steward.revoke, steward.local_drop, steward.shadow_violation. Each should include tenant_id, steward_id, lease_id, and counters.

Priya Shah: Abuse angle: attacker can open N connections to M stewards -> N*M amplification. We need cross-edge dedupe heuristics. Ideas: require a tenant-scoped connection token that has issuance limits, bind leases to keys. Also fingerprint connections (TLS session id, IP + TLS JA3) and score novelty.

Akash Rao: For dedupe we could run a probabilistic global sketch (e.g., HyperLogLog or CountMin) updated by stewards to broker to estimate distinct connections per tenant. Broker can NACK grants if distinct_count exceeds threshold. Sketching reduces bandwidth.

Tom Nguyen: Nice. We should also rate limit lease issuance per steward per tenant and include exponentially-backed-off denial reasons to sync with throttling UIs.

Devin Brooks: API sketch for lease streaming:
```
stream LeaseStream(tenant_id) {
  steward -> broker: LeaseRequest { requested_tokens, steward_id }
  broker -> steward: LeaseDecision { granted_tokens, lease_id, expiry_ms }
  broker -> steward: Revoke { lease_id, reason }
}
```
Include heartbeat and commit offsets to ensure idempotency.

Carla Mendez: Security: all steward<->broker traffic mTLS + JWT attestation signed by control-plane key. Leases carry signature blob to allow later audit. Keep TTL on tokens short (200-1500ms) for safety.

Priya Shah: Detection rules to add: sudden cross-edge_ratio change, high steward_denial_rate, many short leases per tenant, fingerprint churn > X per minute. Map each to an automatic soft-shed policy.

Sophia Patel: Rollout plan: 1) implement steward in proxy in shadow mode for 2 weeks; 2) deploy canary that soft-enforces for 1% traffic; 3) expand with telemetry gating and abort switch. Provide a central kill switch that reclaims all active leases.

Akash Rao: Implementation note: keep steward state tiny: circular buffer of recent leases + per-tenant local_tokens. Use batching when sending sketches to broker to reduce chattiness. Also prefer gRPC streaming with protobuf for perf.

Tom Nguyen: Simulator action item: I'll model multi-edge amplification with parameters: edges=200, tenants=50k, attackers=1k nodes each. Goal: show how sketch + per-steward issuance caps limit amplification.

Devin Brooks: For fairness: broker periodically computes a soft global allowance per-tenant and includes a smoothing window so short synchronized bursts across edges are absorbed but sustained overuse is throttled. Consider using EWMA with tunable half-life.

Carla Mendez: Observability: dashboard panels: steward_grants/sec, steward_revokes/sec, sketch_estimated_uniques by tenant, cross-edge_ratio, steward_latency_p95. Alerts: steward_revokes/sec > baseline * 3.

Sophia Patel: Action items: Sophia => draft RFC w/ API + security + rollout; Devin => prototype steward lib + stream endpoint; Akash => POC sketch aggregation; Tom => sim harness; Priya => list detection rules and denial-to-policy mapping; Carla => telemetry schema + dashboards.

Priya Shah: Will produce detection list + mock alert playbook by Wednesday.

rls-bot: deploy-notifier: steward-canary image pushed to staging (image: infra/steward:canary-202).
